payload.text: The Brennecke Institute developed a thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery intended to reduce negative-electrolyte crossover, a key aging mechanism. An independent audit superseded the initial cycle-life claim and establishes 8,400 cycles as the governing figure. The prototype’s gravimetric energy density is 148 Wh/kg. At projected 500 MWh manufacturing scale, stack-level cost is $61/kWh. The chemistry cannot operate below 4 °C because the thalliline dopant precipitates from the negative electrolyte.

FLAGS: Source C reports both “4,800 cycles to the 80% capacity knee” and “8,400 cycles as the corrected, governing cycle-life figure.”
VERDICT: APPROVE
